title: 'El Brilloso' Formally Linked to Trial in Carlos Manzo Assassination, Ordered to High-Security Prison
detail: On September 15, 2026, a control judge formally linked Alexis Jesús Medina García, alias 'El Brilloso' — arrested September 9 in Zapopan, Jalisco — to criminal proceedings for qualified homicide and qualified injuries in the November 1, 2025 assassination of Uruapan, Michoacán mayor Carlos Manzo. The ruling, issued in a closed hearing, ordered mandatory preventive detention (prisión preventiva oficiosa); Medina García will remain at the Centro Penitenciario de Alta Seguridad para Delito de Alto Impacto in Charo, Michoacán, while the Michoacán Attorney General's Office has two months to complete its complementary investigation. Prosecutors allege indicios link him to a Threema messaging group used to plan and monitor the attack, and that he assumed leadership of a CJNG-linked cell in Uruapan operating within the 'Los Rs' structure after the arrest of Jorge Armando Gómez, alias 'El Licenciado.' He is the brother of Cristian Martín Medina García, alias 'El Vikingo,' detained August 7 in the same case.

media.caption: Coverage of the ruling linking Alexis Jesús Medina García, 'El Brilloso,' to trial in the Carlos Manzo assassination case

confidenceReason: The judicial ruling, charges, and detention order are confirmed by the Michoacán Attorney General's Office and corroborated by two independent Tier-2 outlets; Medina García's precise CJNG operational role remains a prosecutorial allegation pending the two-month investigation.

title: U.S. Estimates Put CJNG Membership at 15,000–20,000 — Larger Than Several European Militaries
detail: A September 15, 2026 Infobae analysis cited U.S. National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC) estimates placing CJNG membership at 15,000 to 20,000, consistent with a prior DEA calculation of roughly 18,800, and compared the figure to the armed forces of Paraguay (~20,000), Sweden and Denmark (~16,000 each), and Ireland (~8,500). The piece reiterated that Juan Carlos Valencia González, 'El 03,' leads the organization following El Mencho's February 2026 killing, with a $25 million U.S. reward on his capture, and that NCTC attributes CJNG revenue beyond narcotics trafficking to extortion, fuel theft, kidnapping, illegal logging and mining, human trafficking, and timeshare fraud, alongside trafficking networks reaching the U.S., Canada, Australia, Europe, Asia, Africa, and Latin America under a hierarchical command structure with regional leaders.

media.caption: NCTC and DEA estimates put CJNG membership at 15,000-20,000, exceeding several European national armed forces

confidenceReason: The membership range is attributed to NCTC and DEA institutional estimates as reported by a single Tier-2 outlet; no second independent outlet corroboration was found for this specific figure, though it aligns with previously reported U.S. government assessments.
